extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research-integrity professionals, journal editors, and readers interested in retractions and research misconduct
extracted.subtask_description: A short news report describing an Office of Research Integrity (ORI) finding of research misconduct, the specific forms of data falsification/fabrication, affected publications and thesis, and ensuing corrections/retractions and sanctions. Useful for tracking cases and understanding common misconduct patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct: falsification and fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaged in research misconduct by knowingly, intentionally, and/or recklessly falsifying and/or fabricating data included in the following four (4) published papers and her Ph.D. Thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the ORI's core finding — data that are knowingly, intentionally, or recklessly falsified or fabricated constitute research misconduct. The finding specifies affected publications and the dissertation; such findings are the basis for institutional and federal actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper image manipulation (Western blots and gels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly, intentionally, and/or recklessly falsified and/or fabricated Western blot data ... by trimming and manipulating Western blot images to disguise their origin or by reversing negative DNA gel images of the PCR product, reusing and relabeling them to represent Western blot data for unrelated experiments in seventeen (17) figures included in four (4) published papers and twelve (12) figures included in her Ph.D. Thesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific flagged practices include trimming/manipulating blot images to disguise origin, reversing gel images, reusing images across unrelated experiments, and relabeling. These image manipulations are identified as direct evidence of falsification/fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of original reliable image data invalidates derived quantitative results
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of original reliable image data, the quantitative data in associated plots, statistical analyses, and related text also are falsified and/or fabricated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If original/raw image data are unavailable or unreliable, any derived numerical results, plotted data, statistics, or text interpretations that depend on those images are considered suspect and may be judged falsified/fabricated. This underscores the importance of preserving original data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for confirmed misconduct (federal funding ban)
rubrics_metrics.description: A four-year ban on receiving federal research funding was imposed by the U.S. Office of Research Integrity (ORI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORI can impose administrative sanctions such as prohibitions on receiving federal funds. Such sanctions follow formal findings of misconduct and have career and funding consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections vs. retractions as journal responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLoS paper was corrected (though not retracted) in 2017. At the recommendation of the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health following an internal review, this article is being corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals may issue corrections when institutional review recommends remediation (e.g., corrected figures/legends). Other affected articles were retracted (listed in the notice). The choice between correction and retraction depends on journal/institutional findings about the severity and impact of the problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should identify affected citations/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The following references cited within this article have been retracted: [lists of retracted papers with citations]. Corrections to this article are as follows: Fig 3 is incorrect because of errors made in the preparation of the images in panels B and C. The corrected figure and legend appear below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction or correction notices provide bibliographic detail of affected works and explain what is being changed (e.g., which figures/legends are incorrect). Clear notice helps readers and databases track and update the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct findings can implicate multiple grants and institutional responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The research was part of a dozen different NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misconduct affecting work funded by multiple grants can have broader implications for funding agencies, institutions, and related projects. Institutional internal reviews may prompt journal actions (corrections/retractions) and federal investigations (e.g., ORI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctoral dissertations are subject to misconduct findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Malhotra's Ph.D. Thesis was specifically named among items containing falsified/fabricated data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings of fabrication/falsification can extend to theses/dissertations in addition to journal publications; institutions and record-keepers may need to address degree status or thesis corrections/notations.
